name: salvage-refused-when-nothing-produced
description: A zstd stream cut before its first block's content ever arrived: it ended early AND produced nothing, so it is refused rather than salvaged.

error.detail: unexpected EOF with no output produced

grounding: Salvage requires two conjuncts, not one: the stream ended early *and* it produced something first. Dropping the second conjunct would land every corrupt capture as a silently empty turn, which reads downstream as a real but contentless turn rather than as a failure. The cut is an absolute byte count, not a ratio, because "nothing was producible" has to be true for every compressor and not just the one that built the fixture: whether a whole block happens to land inside some fraction of the stream is a property of an encoder's block splitting and level, so a ratio would let a conformant decoder fed another encoder's bytes legitimately salvage output and fail a case that is supposed to be about the decoder.
notes: 9 bytes is derived from the zstd frame structure, not from this stream's length: the 4-byte magic, plus the smallest frame header the format allows (2 bytes — a frame-header descriptor and a window descriptor), plus a 3-byte block header. So byte 10 is the earliest position at which any encoder's first byte of block *content* can appear, and a block that has delivered no content can have produced no output — whatever its type. An encoder that writes a larger frame header (up to 14 bytes) or splits differently only pushes that first content byte further out, so the bound holds for all of them. Distinct from error-corrupt-zstd-frame, which is a frame that is malformed rather than merely unfinished.
